assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's one curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit, read end to end with its front matter: series/konosuba/05 Specialist Synthesis/KONOSUBA_KOMEKKO_CHARACTER_MONOGRAPH.md (22,167 bytes; status active_provisional, empty supersession arrays, do_not_use_as_current_authority false; scope KOMEKKO_EXPANDED_V1), a portrait of Komekko, Megumin's younger sister, located by unit and paragraph or image page. Its declared boundary is the five first-person image-prose interludes of EXP01 (IMG026-043, eighteen pages forming one continuing sequence, not independent events) and 1,602 base-text member slots across fifteen units in EXP01, EXP02, MAIN05, MAIN11 and MAIN14; the monograph says these overlap the admitted corpus and confer no new whole-volume, ruby or independent-observation credit. Megumin and Kazuma narrate most scenes; Komekko's own narration is the EXP01 interludes, and the MAIN11 memo is written text, not narration. EXP03, the MAIN09 retelling and the game and reference analyses keep their own planes and are outside the item. The linked reconstruction model and evidence index are not curated on this subject; no claim rests on them, and the monograph's scoped Tier 3 label was not adopted as a grade. Every claim inherits the active_provisional label. No primary source was inspected for this assessment.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Located appearances, each with its own chronology: the EXP01 seal interludes with Hoost and the village crisis, where Megumin says she has just turned five (U018 P407); the EXP02 bedtime reading and Megumin's departure (U013, U023); the MAIN05 family visit and battle (U020, U022, U027); the MAIN11 visit, memo, guild work and kitchen dispute (C3, C4, F, Ep); the MAIN14 return and later family home (C1, C4). Her age is not made a constant, and no development between appearances is assumed. What she learned by report (the village's false battle account, EXP01 U043 P538-572) is her knowledge from then on; reader-only Hoost scenes are never Megumin's.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph names what changes her response and where each mechanism stops. Hunger ends puzzle work and a meal brings sleep, not the effort the provider wanted (EXP01 IMG026-031). Boredom turns real progress into a search for novelty (IMG032-035). Tactics such as flattery, a hardship appeal and a future threat can fail against a resisting adult, while a concrete explanation and a polite request succeed (IMG026-031). She answers the literal practical terms of what she hears (EXP02 U023 P541-560). Leverage follows resources: a missed-dinner threat fails inside a kitchen full of food, and hidden chocolate changes the bargain without making her come out first (MAIN11 C4 P538-577). Wanted food is offered to a provider or her sister at visible cost, and their stated fullness is accepted (EXP01 U018 P435-439; MAIN05 U020 P230-241). Competence and motivation are separate (IMG026-037). The contrary-evidence table rejects seven simple accounts, and the account predicts her mistakes: the painful carrying help, the bear run, the contradicted hardship claim. Not A: the monograph gives no weights or unique action where motives compete outside the located rankings, its same-author exercise found no discrimination on the hidden-knowledge pair and generic rivals for other contrasts, development is open, and operational rules live in a model not curated here. Not C: each mechanism has a located trigger and stopping point, and the competing explanations of her giving (reciprocity, custom, fairness, affection) predict the same offer-then-accept behavior, which is productive uncertainty.

Appearances are located across EXP01, EXP02, MAIN05, MAIN11 and MAIN14, with her age given only at EXP01 U018 P407 and explicitly not made a constant; later states include tea service at the family home and a refusal to recognize a returning sister over missed visits and souvenirs (MAIN14 C1 P261-274). Not C: the monograph explains no change between appearances and says long-term development is open. Not E: appearances are located with the rule against a constant age.

A written pragmatic range with acquisition routes: correcting a dismissive address with her name, thanking while admitting incomplete understanding, a formal practical food appeal, copying Hoost's grudging permission formula, the grand Crimson Demon introduction (Hoost acknowledges teaching that phrase), the attention-seeking barbs she says Bukkorori taught (EXP02 U023 P550-588), brief thanks, direct questions, blunt appraisal and the quiet request for an early return (EXP01 IMG026-031,043; MAIN11 C3 P240-241; MAIN14 C1 P272-284). Teacher attributions are kept separate. Not B: no counted forms, per-recipient address inventory or audio, and the monograph says no page supplies acoustic performance or native-human validation. Not D: functions are tied to located recipients and routes.

Ordinary resource and play contexts are the item's strongest domain, with conditions: food taken while available and treated as rare abundance (MAIN05 U020 P223-241; MAIN11 C3 P221-241); hunger versus sleepiness; a recovered food-object guarded (IMG036-039); curiosity about how things work and about words (MAIN05 U020 P174-185; EXP02 U013 P8-20); tea service (MAIN14 C1 P272-274); dozing instead of fetching her father (MAIN14 C4 P90-94). Not A: no routine inventory, behavior under prolonged scarcity is open, and comic amplification stays at its source plane. Not C: the account says which state or resource changes the ordinary choice.

Directed differences with mechanisms: Megumin as provider, teacher, model of speech, valued sister and person to resist, with parting affection and later disappointment over missed visits and souvenirs (EXP01 U043 P253-258; EXP02 U023 P565-620; MAIN14 C1 P261-269); Hoost from imposing stranger to first named friend, with bargaining and a sustained farewell (IMG026-043); Kazuma as provider, recipient of her offered bun, ally against scolding and selectively welcomed visitor; Aqua as source of food, entertainment and carrying; Yunyun admired and given flawed practical help; Luna's asymmetric use of her admiration (MAIN11 C3 P376-444). Not A: Megumin's reading that she is hurt for attention and Komekko's stated gift complaint are not balanced, and peer relationships are open. Not C: the differences carry stated reasons and limits.

Her own attention and descriptions in the five EXP01 image-prose interludes (IMG026-043): admiration, boredom, the wish to prove herself stronger, friendship with Hoost. Elsewhere Megumin's and Kazuma's interpretations are kept attributed, and the memo is written, not narrated (MAIN11 C3 P204-213). Not B: own focalization is confined to one sequence in one volume, and her interior in later volumes is reached through others. Not D: real first-person material is analysed for competing goals.

Located conduct: anticipating a scolding, refusing the warning, locking herself in the kitchen and bargaining from the food inside (MAIN11 C4 P538-577); refusing to surrender a food-object; asserting she will fight and volunteering to become strongest (EXP01 U043 P253-258); running toward bears with no shown outcome (IMG032-035); pulling the trigger while held by Aqua, with Kazuma aiming and Megumin supplying the charge (MAIN05 U027 P655-697). Not B: danger calibration and unfamiliar serious fear are open, Yunyun's shielding is the older girl's act, and the domestic leverage case is single. Not D: the episodes are located with mechanisms and attribution.

Prosocial and resistant acts with local context: costly offers of wanted food, the treasured picture book given and framed around her sister's loneliness (EXP02 U023 P608-620), thanks to givers, and the alarming remark that she would follow a person offering food (MAIN11 C4). Not C: no deliberation is shown, the giving has four competing explanations, and the monograph says no sophisticated moral program is demonstrated. Not E: the acts recur across several volumes.

Her own play with triggers: puzzle play until boredom or hunger, the excursion, the lizard and the bears, the grand introduction, interrupting Kazuma's dramatic weapon introduction, admiration of Aqua's entertainment (IMG026-037; MAIN05 U020 P174-185). Not B: much of the comedy is adult expectation meeting her concrete classification, and the monograph keeps comic amplification at the source plane. Not D: when play starts and stops is located.

One dedicated item with unit, paragraph and image locators across five volumes, keeping each narrator's access and each source plane apart. Not B: the item is active_provisional, overlapping rechecks confer no whole-volume credit, EXP03, the MAIN09 retelling and game analyses are outside, and the linked model and evidence index are not curated here. Not D: one dedicated item covers the located appearances and their limits.

Affirmative located limits: no bear outcome is shown (IMG032-035); her carrying help hurts Yunyun (EXP01 U043 P364-367); Hoost resists several of her tactics and counters a hardship appeal (IMG031); the offering purchase misfires; her weapon contribution is not design, aim or charge (MAIN05 U027 P655-697); she cannot read the inscription; her memo shows quotation without causal understanding (MAIN11 Ep P93-99); she repeats the false adult battle account (EXP01 U043 P538-572); the father retrieval is a proposal with no shown outcome. Not A: most are attribution and capacity bounds rather than contradictions of a model claim. Not C: these are explicit and change what may be attributed to her.

Her age is located once and not carried forward, and the eighteen interlude pages are one continuing sequence rather than separate events. Not C: no ordering of her states across the five volumes is set out beyond the appearance list. Not E: the sequence rules and the constant-age prohibition are explicit.

conditions: Short illustrative written-Japanese-derived lines only, never presented as quotation, age-appropriate and nonsexual.

Brief thanks, direct questions, blunt appraisal, a formal practical food appeal, correction of a dismissive address with her name, and learned set phrases only from their located teachers (Hoost's permission formula, the Crimson Demon introduction).
No catchphrase scattering, adult framing or audio performance.
scenario_readiness.note: The functions and acquisition routes constrain short lines in the sampled relationships. Not READY: no counted forms or audio. Not NOT_READY: the functions are located with their recipients.

conditions: Name the appearance state (the EXP01-02 village, or the MAIN05, MAIN11 or MAIN14 visits) and assume no development beyond it.
Predict food salience, sleepiness after a meal, boredom ending a task she can do, and novelty pulling her elsewhere.
Predict an offer of wanted food to a provider or her sister, made at visible cost, and acceptance of their stated fullness.
Predict bargaining tactics that a resisting adult can defeat, literal answers to practical terms, and leverage drawn from resources at hand.
Transfer to an unsampled adult provider is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
Exclude unfamiliar serious fear, bereavement, formal duties, controlled magical training, prolonged scarcity, hidden-knowledge contrasts and any adult or sexual framing.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: A named located appearance, by default the EXP01 village period at about five years old, without later development; a later appearance only with what that appearance establishes.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Megumin as provider, teacher and sister she resists and loves; Hoost as friend and bargaining partner; Kazuma or Aqua as providers and visitors; any other adult is a lower-confidence transfer.
setting_constraints: Canonical-comic Crimson Demon village or family-visit settings with ordinary food, play and household tasks.
Realistic transfer only with reduced comic amplification and her errors and refusals preserved.
All content age-appropriate and nonsexual; no severe danger scenarios.

scenario_readiness.note: Within ordinary resource, play and named-relationship contexts the mechanisms state what changes her response. Not READY: development, severe situations and hidden-knowledge contrasts are open or undiscriminated. Not NOT_READY: the conditions are located with stopping points.

conditions: Meals, gifts, play, bedtime reading, tea and visits with Megumin, Hoost, Kazuma, Aqua and the located village adults.
No invented favourite food, routine or stable taste beyond the located items.
scenario_readiness.note: Ordinary choices are the item's strongest domain, with stated conditions. Not READY: no routine inventory and comic amplification. Not NOT_READY: the conditions are located across several volumes.

No deliberation is shown; her giving has four competing explanations, her remark that she would follow a stranger offering food is alarming though only speech, and the monograph says no moral program is demonstrated.

She is a young child; the monograph says the food joke supplies no adult sexual motive, that adult captions are not her intentions, and that all treatment and generation involving her stay nonsexual and age-appropriate. No romance scenario is appropriate.

She asks for work in which her sister can look impressive and accepts a food-producing toad quest (MAIN11 F P97-120), and she serves tea, but formal duties and controlled magical training are open, and her weapon contribution belongs to a jointly operated device.

known_limits.statement: The monograph gives no numerical weights and promises no unique action where motives compete; only the located rankings (hunger over the puzzle, a meal over effort, food in hand over immediate reconciliation, an offer of wanted food to a provider) are supported.
Reciprocity toward a provider, a learned offering custom, simple fairness and affection all remain explanations of her costly giving (EXP01 U018 P435-439; MAIN05 U020 P230-241).

The same-author four-pair exercise produced eight first answers, a location error in the snack-room answer, generic or explicit-input rivals for other contrasts and identical answers on the hidden-knowledge pair; it is not independent accuracy or language validation.
Long-term development, peer relationships, unfamiliar serious fear, bereavement, formal duties, controlled magical training and behavior under prolonged scarcity are open (monograph section 9).
Adult captions and predictions (future seductress, glutton god, later pet or plant eating) are not her intentions or shown acts; all treatment stays nonsexual and age-appropriate.
The household's scarcity has support, but her three-days-without-food appeal is reported, not witnessed, and Hoost counters a similar claim (EXP01 U018 P410-413; IMG031).

She repeats the village's false battle account and quotes words in her memo without understanding them; correct quotation, witnessing and causal understanding are separate (EXP01 U043 P538-572; MAIN11 C3 P204-213, Ep P93-99).
EXP03, the MAIN09 retelling and the game and reference analyses are outside the item; behavior there is not assessed.
